thread:
sam: Customer (acme) reporting p99 ~18s and intermittent 502/504s since 15:03 UTC in hosted-prod-us-east-1. Customer supplied sample req id=01FZQ7A2. They say calls that previously were 300-500ms are timing out. I'm seeing a big jump in ingress queue depth for tenant=acme and a bunch of 429s forwarded to them. Raising to eng now :rotating_light:

anya: Looking at dashboards — ingress queue depth spiked at 15:02, worker pool worker-pool-12 CPU at 98%, auth-db connection waiters increasing. Auth DB pool reports "max_clients=50 connections=50 waiting=14". This looks like auth-db saturation + worker overload causing longer admission wait times. Repro: curl to host with sample req returns 504 after 12s of queue wait.

mike: I can triage. Quick mitigation plan: 1) temporarily increase per-tenant concurrency for acme to reduce queueing 2) move their traffic to warm workers (bypass warmup routing) 3) enable model-fallback to smaller variant to drop CPU per request. I'll run steps 1+2 now.

mike: command I will run (API-driven):
```
# bump concurrency limit for tenant acme (admin only)
curl -X POST "https://internal-api.redwood/v1/admin/tenants/acme/overrides" \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDWOOD_ADMIN_TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"concurrency_limit": 40, "route_override": "warm-workers"}'
```

mike: quick logs snapshot from worker-pool-12: 
```
[15:04:12] worker[12] ERROR AdmissionTimeout tenant=acme req=01FZQ7A2 wait_ms=12000
[15:04:12] auth-db ERROR pool exhausted: max_clients=50 connections=50 waiting=14
[15:04:13] worker[12] WARN KVCache miss tenant=acme key=conv_98
```

deploy-bot: started rollout -> config-admin/tenant-overrides (id: ro-20260317-51). patching route assignment for tenant=acme -> warm-workers. status: in-progress.

anya: After bump, ingress queue depth dropped ~60% in the warm pool and p95 improved from ~2.4s to ~820ms for the sampled requests. Auth DB waiters still present but fewer timeouts. We should follow up: 1) increase auth-db pool or add read-replica for auth queries 2) investigate KV cache churn for acme (hot keys) 3) run a short-term canary for model-fallback to ensure output quality.

sam: I'll update customer with current mitigations and ETA (~15–20m for steady state). Marking this P2 and creating a support-ticket with logs + sample req id. Thanks all.

mike: filing an eng-runtime ticket to track follow-ups (link: https://tickets.redwood/ENG-rt/987). tagging for postmortem if p99 regresses again.

sam: noted. I'll add the customer's SLA note and keep them patched in.
